2. **[Compute]** (Estimator consistency) A qualification campaign runs `{python} MemoryProblems.n_runs_str` ground-truth runs on the scalar rack-end distance and finds a mean NEES of `{python} MemoryProblems.nees_obs_str` (illustrative). Compute the 95 percent acceptance band, state the verdict, and say whether the filter's clearance claims are too wide or too narrow. How many runs would be needed before a mean NEES of `{python} MemoryProblems.nees_test_str` falls outside the band, and what does that count imply for a campaign that wants to detect mild overconfidence?

3. **[Compute]** (Tracking and occupancy) The tracker confirms identity by a `{python} MemoryProblems.m_confirm_str`-of-`{python} MemoryProblems.n_confirm_str` rule on the navigation camera. Give the shortest and longest confirmation intervals after the first detection, and the base's travel at its `{python} RackEndBelief.v_drive_str` drive limit over the `{python} RackEndBelief.t_age_str` frame age plus the longest interval. 4. **[Compute]** (Transform composition) A longer tool puts the fingertip `{python} MemoryProblems.lever_new_str` beyond the wrist (illustrative). Using the chapter's latch-slot values, compute the finger error after one stale wrist-camera frame on a hand-composed chain, and the longest lever arm for which one stale frame still fits the `{python} LatchTransformStaleness.e_max_str` slot. What does the same-time composition of the belief's growth law give over one frame with the longer tool, and why does the lever arm drop out?

5. **[Compute]** (Localization drift) The site allots `{python} MemoryProblems.loc_share_str` of the `{python} OdometryDrift.delta_loc_str` localization bound to odometry drift between map corrections (chosen). With the UMBmark rates of @fig-09-odometry-drift, find the longest distance between corrections, calibrated and uncalibrated, and the calibrated interval in seconds at the `{python} OdometryDrift.v_aisle_str` aisle speed. A loop closure then moves the supporting poses by `{python} MemoryProblems.d_closure_str` (illustrative). What happens to a snapshot copied before the closure whose cells still pass every age check, and what must the host do?

6. **[Design]** (Representation choice) With the arm extended the machine needs `{python} MemoryProblems.n_hulls_new_str` sphere hulls (illustrative) inside the same `{python} MemoryProblems.t_reflex_str` collision-checking allocation of @eq-mem-query-latency-budget. Recompute the per-query time and read budget on the permission controller, and decide which representation and pitch of @tbl-09-representation-queries and @fig-09-memory-3d-representation-pareto still certify a hull. For your choice, give the snapshot storage and the quantization error charged against the `{python} RackEndBelief.delta_margin_str` protective clearance, and name the measurement that would qualify the query bound.

7. **[Compute]** (Representation cost) The host adds a second depth camera and integrates both at the `{python} MemoryProblems.pitch_fine_str` manipulation pitch (`{python} MemoryProblems.n_streams_str` streams, illustrative). Using @eq-mem-dram-bandwidth and the chapter's stream parameters, compute the naive ray-marching traffic and its share of the host's peak DRAM bandwidth, and the dense-grid footprint of the chapter's workcell at that pitch and at 2 cm. Decide which one forces a design change, and what the change is.

8. **[Design]** (Negative evidence and cell epochs) A scan down the aisle crosses cells `{python} MemoryProblems.d_cell_a_str`, `{python} MemoryProblems.d_cell_b_str`, and `{python} RackEndBelief.d_clear_str` from the unobserved cross-aisle boundary and ends on a tote face; the cross aisle itself stays hidden. Specify the fields each cell carries and the update the return applies to cells before, at, and behind the tote. Compute when each crossed cell reverts from free to unknown by @eq-mem-free-space-expiry, and state what a later map publication does to those deadlines.

9. **[Compute]** (Belief expiry) Recompute the latch-slot horizon of @fig-uncertainty-growth with the disturbance bound doubled and then halved (chosen), and the ratio of each horizon to the chapter's. Explain why the change is not proportional. Then find the smallest free-space depth at which the rack-end claim still survives the frame's `{python} RackEndBelief.t_age_str` dispatch age, and say what that depth means for where along the aisle memory helps at all.

10. **[Compute]** (Belief expiry, transfer to a logistics AMR) An autonomous mobile robot without an arm approaches the same rack end at its `{python} MemoryProblems.amr_v_str` registry drive limit, with the warehouse machine's localization bound and protective clearance. A hull that advances toward the unobserved boundary while that boundary erodes toward the hull meets it sooner than the static root of @eq-mem-free-space-expiry. Derive the time at which a hull starting `{python} RackEndBelief.d_clear_str` from the boundary loses its certified depth for the AMR and for the warehouse machine at its `{python} OdometryDrift.v_aisle_str` aisle speed, and subtract the frame age. Then give the largest record skew each machine tolerates under the conservative envelope of the skewed-records pitfall. Which registry value does the AMR still lack before its stop can be checked against this interval?

11. **[Critique]** (Belief expiry) A teammate proposes one `{python} MemoryProblems.t_timeout_str` staleness timeout for every belief, arguing that it is simpler to qualify than four growth laws. Using @tbl-09-belief-decay-horizons, compute each row's error bound at the timeout and whether the timeout over-admits or under-admits that belief. Write the critique, and state what a per-belief expiry costs the team in exchange.

12. **[Critique]** (Diagnosing silent failures) A vendor states that its tracker's innovation monitor catches both frozen transforms and sensor bias drift. For the frozen-transform timeline of @sec-memory-failure-modes, compute the error the publish-time check admits after `{python} MemoryFrozenTransform.t_window_str` ms and the largest error a `{python} MemoryFrozenTransform.tau_max_str` ms age check on the capture epoch would admit. For the strain-gauge case, give the innovation during the drift and the number of samples the `{python} MemoryBiasDrift.t_excite_str` ms contact break provides at `{python} MemoryBiasDrift.f_sample_str` Hz. Critique the claim, naming for each failure the check that actually exposes it and the lifecycle state it should force.


::: {.callout-chapter-connection title="From valid beliefs to bounded goals"}
What may a valid belief authorize? Memory rules only on validity. It can say that a remembered object lies within a stated bound until a stated deadline, but it cannot say what the machine should do about that object. In the intent layer, a human goal, taking the mug from the conveyor, becomes an intent lease that consumes the belief record of the mug's handle, carries that belief's evidence epoch forward as its own evidence time, caps its expiry at that belief's horizon, and grants a bounded target with effort limits, never a path, for no longer than the evidence beneath it supports.
:::
